stem: How many of the firm's employees are part-time?
stimulus: A labour economist studying staffing patterns finds that a logistics firm has 240 employees. Each employee is full-time, part-time, or on a fixed-term contract. If one employee is selected at random, the probability of selecting a full-time employee is 0.6. If one of the employees who are not full-time is selected at random, the probability of selecting a contract employee is 0.375.
explanation: There are $0.6 \times 240 = 144$ full-time employees, which leaves $240 - 144 = 96$ who are not full-time. Of those 96, $0.375 \times 96 = 36$ are contract employees. That means $96 - 36 = 60$ are part-time.

B.why: You applied 0.375 to the 144 full-time employees. The second probability describes the employees who are not full-time, so you should multiply it by 96.

D.why: You found the 96 employees who are not full-time. That group includes the contract employees too, and you still need to remove them.
